title: Southwest Research analysis of the implant sliver
place_text: Southwest Research Institute, San Antonio, Texas

tellings.quote: Bill says, "I've got your piece of your sliver of the implant." And he [clears throat] says it is um a metal metallic base with febrow motion moving uh uh celia coming off of it.

plain: In the mid-1990s, a sliver of what Whitley Strieber calls his implant is said to have been examined at the Southwest Research Institute in San Antonio, Texas, and found to be a metal base with tiny fibres, like cilia, coming off it and moving. Strieber, a writer who says he has met non-human beings, tells Michels what a man there named William Malow told him: "I've got your piece of your sliver of the implant." If true, the object would have a living-seeming structure no ordinary metal fragment has.
